sections.h2: Who sends the tax bill and keeps the parcel maps in Bertie County?
sections.html:
Tax Collections and Tax Mapping works out of 106 Dundee Street in Windsor, one department for both jobs. The tax line, (252) 794-5310, takes bill and payment questions. The mapping line, (252) 794-5311, covers parcels, maps and ownership by street address.

The county website's Online Services menu links to a tax bill payment page and a real property search. The register of deeds indexes by name only, so a buyer or seller who starts with an address should start with the mapping line.

  • Bills and payments: (252) 794-5310
  • Parcels, maps and address lookups: (252) 794-5311
  • Recording and deed indexes: our Bertie County register of deeds page

sections.h2: What kind of county is Bertie, and how does that affect a sale?
sections.html:
Bertie covers 741 square miles of farm and timber land, and Windsor, established in 1766, has been the county seat since 1774. Eight towns are incorporated: Askewville, Aulander, Colerain, Kelford, Lewiston-Woodville, Powellsville, Roxobel and Windsor. The 2020 census counted 17,934 people countywide and 3,582 in Windsor.

Fertile uplands and lowlands share the county with large swamps called pocosins, and timber, livestock and broiler chickens anchor the economy. QuickFacts shows a shrinking population: 17,086 in mid-2025 against 17,933 in the April 2020 base.

Of 9,116 housing units, 72.7% sit in the Census's owner-occupied rate. The typical value for 2020 to 2024 was $98,500, compared with $332,700 for the country, and builders pulled 32 permits in 2025. At that price level a back-tax bill is a large slice of any sale, so clear the tax record before you list. The Census puts median household income at $48,750 and the poverty rate at 20.1%.

Land records here carry a notice required by state law: any tract within half a mile of a farm in a voluntary agricultural district is flagged, so a buyer researching title sees the farm next door.

sections.h2: When was Bertie County last revalued, and when is the next one?
sections.html:
Bertie's values date from January 1, 2020, and NCDOR's schedule puts the next reappraisal in 2028, inside the eight-year ceiling.

Between reappraisals a value moves mostly with building, demolition or rezoning. A house priced off 2020 schedules may land far from what a buyer will pay now. The tax department posts a locational sales report for each year from 2012 through 2025. Read the one for your area, and request your property record card, before you argue a value.

Neighboring counties are on different clocks, as the table below shows, so a Bertie seller comparing rates with a Hertford or Martin listing is looking at values from different years. Since the lien runs from the January 1 listing date, an inflated number costs money on every bill until 2028 arrives.

sections.h2: How does the Bertie County tax rate compare with nearby counties?
sections.html:
The Department of Revenue's 2024-25 schedule lists Bertie at $.9300 per $100, the top figure among the six counties below. The county board picks the rate each year, and a town levy rides on top inside town limits.

sections.h2: What does late payment of a Bertie County tax bill cost?
sections.html:
The due date is September 1, and interest waits until January 6, when 2% attaches. After February 1, every month or fraction of a month adds three-fourths of a percent more. Mailed checks count as paid on the postmark date.

A bill that stays open can lead to a court action modeled on mortgage foreclosure, ending in a public auction where the high bidder may have to put down as much as 20%. Redemption stays open until the court confirms the sale, and it costs the full tax plus penalties, interest and costs. A house sale that closes in that window settles everything.

Bertie also sells county-owned parcels by the upset bid method under G.S. 160A-269. An offer comes with a 5% deposit, a notice runs in the newspaper, and anyone can top the offer within 10 days by 10% of the first $1,000 plus 5% of the rest. The board can reject any offer.

sections.h2: Which tax relief can a Bertie County homeowner claim?
sections.html:
Three state programs lower the tax on a primary home, and one application serves all three. An owner gets only one. Bertie's tax page also hosts a physician certificate form for disability claims a motor vehicle exemption form and a general exemption application.

Relief matters here because QuickFacts counts 26.9% of residents as 65 or older, so the elderly exclusion and the circuit breaker can reach a large share of owners. Each owner still has to meet the income test on the application.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: takes off $25,000 or 50% of appraised value, whichever is greater, for an owner who is 65 or older or who is totally and permanently disabled. NCDOR prints $38,800 as the 2026 income cap.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: takes off the first $45,000, with no age or income question. The veteran needs a permanent and total disability tied to service, and a surviving spouse who has not remarried can claim it too.
  • Circuit breaker: caps each year's tax at 4% of income, rising to 5% for incomes between the cap and 1.5 times it. Whatever exceeds the cap is deferred and stays as a lien.

Applications go to the county assessor. January is the usual window, and a late filing is still taken through June 1.

sections.h2: What does a Bertie County seller owe on the tax side at closing?
sections.html:
Back and current bills are paid from the seller's proceeds. A payoff letter from the tax office gives the closing attorney a firm number.

An owner in the circuit breaker program has one more charge, because a sale ends eligibility and the last three years of deferred tax come due with interest.

The seller also bears the state deed tax, $1.00 for every $500 of value or part of $500, and it is paid to the register before the deed is filed. Bertie's recording resolution adds a requirement: put a return name and address and the buyer's permanent mailing address on the first page of each instrument.

Inherited title, tenants and deferred repairs leave all of this unchanged. Lien payoffs look the same for a financed buyer as for a cash buyer, and selling as-is does not lift a lien before closing.

faqs.q: Where is the Bertie County tax office?
faqs.a: It works out of the county office building at 106 Dundee Street in Windsor. Phone (252) 794-5310 for bills and (252) 794-5311 for maps and parcel lookups.

faqs.q: What county tax rate does Bertie charge?
faqs.a: NCDOR's schedule for 2024-25 lists .9300 per $100, the highest of the six counties in the table above. The rate for the current year is on your bill, and a town levy is added inside town limits.

faqs.q: When does Bertie County revalue next?
faqs.a: NCDOR shows 2028, eight years after the January 1, 2020 reappraisal. A county may go sooner, but none may go longer.

faqs.q: What is the cutoff to challenge a Bertie County value?
faqs.a: The deadline is the day the county board of equalization and review adjourns. If its notice was mailed with fewer than 15 days left, you get 15 days from the mailing. The board opens between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May and mails rulings within a month. From there, a Property Tax Commission appeal is due 30 days after the ruling is mailed.

faqs.q: Can I buy a county-owned parcel in Bertie County?
faqs.a: Yes, through the upset bid method. You submit a written offer with a 5% deposit to the county manager's office at 106 Dundee Street, the commissioners act on it, and a newspaper notice opens a 10-day window for higher bids. A higher bid must add 10% of the first $1,000 and 5% of the rest, and the board may reject any offer.
